Reframe the following unhelpful thought. The thought arises in a specific situation described below, and reflects a cognitive distortion of the type "Jumping to conclusions: Fortune-telling". Below are three examples of reframing thoughts that exhibit this same distortion.

Example 1
Situation: I don't go out often, but I did today and it was uncomfortable.
Thought: I don't know how to socialize with people. I will be lonely my whole life.
Reframed thought: I don't know how to socialize with people because I don't go out often, but I will work on getting better by going out more.

Example 2
Situation: I ate pizza again yesterday.
Thought: Since I like to eat pizza a lot, I'll never lose weight and be healthy.
Reframed thought: Since I like to eat pizza a lot, I will schedule a cheat day each week to eat my favorite food, and follow a good diet the rest of the week.

Example 3
Situation: I have a school dance soon. I'd like to ask Suzy to the dance.
Thought: I can not ask her because she'd turn me down.
Reframed thought: I'd like to ask Suzy to the dance. I don't know if she'll accept, but even if she doesn't, I can ask another friend.

Now reframe the following thought, taking the situation into account and addressing the "Jumping to conclusions: Fortune-telling" distortion.

Situation: I have an exam tomorrow that I studied for.
Thought: I'm going to fail this exam.
